::: {#rem-partial-f-lrt}
#### The partial F-test and the likelihood ratio test

Let the errors be Gaussian.
The maximum likelihood estimate of the error variance of a model with residual sum of squares $\text{RSS}$
is $\text{RSS} / n$,
so its maximized log-likelihood is
$-\tfrac{n}{2} \log(2\pi\, \text{RSS} / n) - \tfrac{n}{2}$.
The [likelihood ratio statistic](intro-MLEs.qmd#def-lrt-stat) of $H_0$ is then

$$
\begin{aligned}
  \lrstat
  &= 2\paren{\llik(\hthml) - \llik(\hparam_0)} \\
  &= n \log \frac{\text{RSS}_0}{\text{RSS}_1} \\
  &= n \log\paren{1 + \frac{\text{RSS}_0 - \text{RSS}_1}{\text{RSS}_1}}.
\end{aligned}
$$

For large $n$ under $H_0$, the ratio $(\text{RSS}_0 - \text{RSS}_1) / \text{RSS}_1$ is near $0$,
so $\log(1 + u) \approx u$ gives
$\lrstat \approx n (\text{RSS}_0 - \text{RSS}_1) / \text{RSS}_1$.
Also $q F = (n - p - 1) (\text{RSS}_0 - \text{RSS}_1) / \text{RSS}_1$,
which is close to the same value when $n$ is much larger than $p$.
Both statistics therefore have approximately the $\chi^2_q$ distribution,
but the F-test is exact for Gaussian errors at every $n$,
while the likelihood ratio test is only approximate.
:::
